reason: The text demonstrates King Saul's antagonistic behavior toward his own people through multiple actions: (1) He imposes a rash oath cursing anyone who eats before evening, which weakens his own army's ability to fight effectively; (2) He condemns his own son Jonathan to death (מוֹת יָמוּת - 'surely he shall die') for unknowingly violating this oath, despite Jonathan's military victory being the cause of Israel's success; (3) The Hebrew people must actively intercede and ransom Jonathan from Saul's judgment (וַיִּפְדּוּ הָעָם אֶת־ יוֹנָתָן - 'the people ransomed Jonathan'), indicating Saul's will runs counter to their welfare. Saul prioritizes legalistic adherence to his oath over the welfare and military success of his own people, demonstrating clear antagonism toward their interests.
